name: Discovery and Registration
problem: A published asset nobody can find is rebuilt by every domain that needs it, and an asset used without a catalogue entry has no recorded owner to contact when it fails.
forces: Registration must be a publication gate, not a post-hoc documentation chore.
Draft assets must be excluded from the index without blocking their development.
Catalogue metadata rots unless registration is enforced rather than encouraged.
solution: Every published asset registers in a central discovery index with owner, description, schema, classification, SLOs, contact information, and consumption instructions. Registration is a prerequisite for publication. Unregistered assets are invisible to consumers and must not be used for cross-domain sharing; draft assets are excluded from the index.

appliesTo.guidance: data-mesh.config.json declares hasDiscoveryRegistration=true; registration precedes publication. Enforced by DAM-R09.
The runtime analogue is the service registry with health-checked instances.

relationships.note: What is registered is a product, with an owner and an SLA.

enforcedBy.statement: All data products SHOULD register in a central data catalog (hasDiscoveryRegistration=true) with owner, description, schema, SLO, and consumption instructions.
